evidence: Cic. Cat. 1.30: in perpetuum comprimī (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The plain prose phrase for something that will last, or be done, for good.
Constantly, continually, and so for ever.
For ever without end: the phrase of prayer and of the psalms (aeternus, without beginning or end). in sempiternum is the same (Vulg. Deut., Lewis & Short s.v. sempiternus).
“Always” (see always): with a future verb it says “for ever”: semper manēbit (Cato in Gell. 16.1, Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: effinge aliquid et excūde, quod sit perpetuō tuum
phrases.english: shape and hammer out something that will be yours for ever

phrases.latin: nōbīs cum semel occidit brevis lūx, nox est perpetua ūna dormienda
phrases.english: for us, once our brief light has set, there is one everlasting night to be slept
the truth of the Lord endures for ever
